newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts stuck in narrow range, 113-17 to cap.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts stuck in narrow range, 113-17 to cap.

text.p: September gilts must cling above 112-31 if they are to grind higher on Tuesday, technical analysts said.
But near term resistance at 113-06, 113-09 then 113-17 will ensure a muted performance, they added.
"Gilts have been hanging on quite well to the 113 area -- an obvious support area is at 113-00/04 to around 112-31," said David Wood, an independent technical analyst near London.
"It wouldn't look good to go through there...as it would open up a move down to 111-30 again." Wood added the market would target 112-21/19 on the way down.

Daily charts show the market bounced off lows of 112-31 on Monday and Friday and off 113-00 on Thursday. It also shrank back from resistance at 113-17 on Friday and 113-16 on Monday, keeping the contract confined to a narrow range.
"The market just looks a bit sick at the moment and it needs something to generate some upside, otherwise it looks like it will contiune slipping, but without any real pace," said Wood.
He said the market would do well to get up to 113-17 on Tuesday, but added it must vault a band of resistance at 113-06, Monday's close, to 113-09 first.
Chase technical analyst Guenter Redeker agreed 112-31 was the key level to hold on Tuesday. He said above there, the market would target 113-26, and below there, 112-17.

"A daily closing price above 114-06 is required to re-test last week's 114-18 high and if above here it will move to 114-31, represented by the contract high traded in May," Redeker said in a note for clients.
By 0709 GMT, September gilts were down 5/32 at 113-01. December short sterling was down one basis point at 92.75.
